paragraphs: Rabbah bar Avuha. He was in Mahoza. He encountered Elijah in the cemetery and asked, “Is the master not a priest?” In their discussion about studying the orders of the Mishnah, Rabbah answered, “I cannot manage four. Can I manage six?” He was poor, and Elijah gave him leaves from the Garden of Eden. The cloak absorbed their fragrance, and he sold it for twelve thousand gold dinars (Bava Metzia 114b). The cited passage says he divided the proceeds among his sons-in-law. He encountered Elijah and asked, “Whose view did Esther follow in inviting Haman?” Elijah answered, “All the tannaim and amoraim” (Megillah 15b, cited as 76b by Heilprin). Rav Nahman's teacher: Tosafot, Eruvin 59, end of b; Gittin 32a. Rav Nahman asked him: Berakhot 21a. Rav Nahman said that Rabbah bar Avahu said that Rav said: Eruvin 75b; there 85a, Shabbat 129b, several statements; Bava Metzia 99a; Zevahim 44, end of b; Keritot 18a. Rav Nahman said that Rabbah bar Avuha said: Gittin 79a, two statements; Eruvin 77b, three statements; Shabbat 64a. He wished to give his daughter to Rav Nahman and ordered that they examine whether his flesh emitted vapor (see there). He became ill, and Rav Huna and Rav Nahman visited him: Gittin 72a; Bava Batra 136a. He said, ‘An incident involving a woman who came before R' Yishmael’: Hagigah 20a. A woman cursed him (Gittin 35a, where the checked text names Rabbah bar Rav Huna). See there. He asked Hiyya bar Rav: Avodah Zarah 51a. R' Hama was his son. Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak in his name. He reported a teaching of Rav Sheshet (Keritot 24a), though another reading there names R’ Abbahu as the transmitter. Rami bar Abba (see there).
